answer: A falcon-eyed verifier checks each agent's history of completed, verifiable work before it may transact: reputation is earned task by task, never granted at signup. A hollow identity with no work record is worthless, no matter how many copies an attacker spawns, because every fake must pay the full cost of real work to gain standing. Cheap copies only echo each other, identical histories with no independent proof, and the network discounts echoes, so a thousand fakes cost a thousand times the work while an honest agent pays once.
